ai.description: This lizard reaches 8–10 cm in snout-vent length. It is olive-brown with a pale throat and lacks a distinct nuchal crest. A short tail and granular scales distinguish this species from congeners.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Coryphophylax brevicauda* is uniquely distinguished from other Indian agamids by its exceptionally short tail, which is significantly shorter than its snout-vent length.
ai.habitat: *Coryphophylax brevicauda* inhabits the dense, humid tropical evergreen forests of the Andaman Islands, typically found on tree trunks within low-to-mid altitudinal ranges.
ai.behavior: The Short-tailed Bay Island Forest Lizard is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small invertebrates along the forest floor and low-lying vegetation during the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Coryphophylax brevicauda* is oviparous, laying clutches of 2–4 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from May to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Coryphophylax brevicauda* is endemic to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands in India, where it inhabits tropical forest environments at low to moderate elevations.
